key_insight: Entity recognition—not knowledge recall—is the main bottleneck in knowledge-based visual question answering, and distinctive visual clues help more than general scene descriptions.
engineering_relevance: Training VLMs to seek identifying visual details can improve recognition and downstream reasoning by better using existing knowledge.
method: Analyze recognition versus knowledge-recall failures in thinking VLMs.
Introduce ClueRL, extending GRPO with an advantage localized to entity-recall clues in reasoning traces.
Train on entity recognition and evaluate transfer to visual question answering and multimodal reasoning.
evidence_signal: Across four models on ViQuAE, misrecognition caused 76.3% of errors; ClueRL outperformed GRPO and a perception-reward baseline on three recognition benchmarks and improved Qwen3.5-4B by 4.4 and 4.0 points on MMStar’s ScienceQA and MMMU subsets.
watch_item: Implementation depends on reliably locating entity-recall clues in reasoning traces; the abstract does not specify that procedure or its cost.
paper_title: Find the Clue, Not the Scene: Rethinking Reasoning for Entity Recognition in Vision-Language Models
